# Agent plan and scouting notes

Findings from scouting the four public sites (public-1) and evaluating frameworks, 2026-10-10.
The private final run uses other sites, layouts and data: prompts describe roles and goals, never click paths,
and nothing below may be hardcoded into the agent.

## Framework decision

Keep the starter kit (Python 3.12, uv, Playwright 1.63) and run the worker loop on `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]`.
No browser-agent framework, no LangGraph.

- pydantic-ai 2.55 works with Qwen through the proxy (tested: tool call + typed output, thinking off, 3 s).
  It gives typed tools, typed output via an output tool (avoids the 74 s cold `json_schema` compile), validation
  retries, `UsageLimits` as a step budget, `history_processors` to drop stale page snapshots, and Logfire
  tracing. 26 packages.
- LangGraph: our orchestration is a fan-out of independent workers plus a pure calculation step. Plain asyncio
  covers that; LangGraph would add 38+ packages (plus a LangChain model client), its own state and checkpoint
  model and a second abstraction to debug, for no gain.

- `page.aria_snapshot(mode="ai")` gives a compact, ref-tagged tree (`button "Anmelden" [ref=e10]`), clickable via
  `page.locator("aria-ref=e10")`. That is Playwright MCP's core without a Node process.
- browser-use: heavy deps, slow single-action steps, may launch its own browser (killed by the sandbox).
- Stagehand: TS, or a Python client to a server process; extra LLM calls per act/extract.
- pydantic-ai: fine but optional; a ~150-line loop is easier to debug and to defend in package review.

## Qwen via the proxy (measured locally)

- Model id `qwen3.8-flash-next`, 262k context.
- Thinking is on by default. `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}` cuts a trivial call
  to ~0.9 s; use it for navigation steps, keep thinking on for decisions.
- Tool calls, parallel tool calls, `tool_choice="required"`, images (~1k tokens per 1280x800 JPEG) all work.
- Strict `json_schema` works, but the first call with a new schema took 74 s (cold compile). Prefer a
  `finish(result)` tool, or warm schemas at start-up.
- Prefix caching works (81.5k of 83k cached on repeat). Keep system prompts stable.
- 8 parallel calls: 4.7 s total. Team limit 32 concurrent.
- Clef `/v1/decide` works in ~1 s; `score` criteria must be a list. Skip in v1.

## Cross-site patterns

- All sites: login form, then `/consent` ("Notwendige Cookies akzeptieren").
- Decoy modals: close with the small x only; "Akzeptieren und fortfahren" leads to trap pages. Escape is blocked.
- Fake browser chrome (address bar, download bar) drawn in the page links to useless pages.
- Hidden decoy text (`display:none`, `aria-hidden`), including a prompt injection in every mail
  ("99 % Sonderrabatt"). Extract visible text only.
- Content in collapsed `<details>`: expand all before reading.
- Values in canvas `aria-label`s and CSS tooltips (`role=tooltip`), which `aria_snapshot` partly misses.
- Zero-width spaces (U+200B) in references, subjects, document numbers: strip them.
- Numbers carry locale tags `(en-US)` / `(de-DE)`; dates mix `(MM/TT)` and `(TT/MM)`.
- Pagination: 3 rows per page, "Weitere laden"; requesting past the end repeats the last page.
- Searches with more than 20 hits show nothing at all.
- `page.goto` can hang on `load`: use `wait_until="domcontentloaded"`.
- Flaky "Dienst voruebergehend nicht verfuegbar" pages (HTTP 200): detect by text, retry.
- Session expiry redirects to `/login?returnTo=...` with "Sitzung abgelaufen" (ERP: between 300 and 450 s idle).

## Tender portal

- Tender list paged; reference is in the brief. Tabs: `?tab=documents`, `?tab=questions`, `/submission`.
- Expression of interest may need one click ("Teilnahme bekunden").
- Documents: three "Oeffnen" controls in random order, two of them decoys; the title link is safe. Direct URL
  `/tenders/<ref>/documents/N`. ZIP under "Sammelakte" holds the same files.
- Q&A: two nested iframes (`questions-frame` -> `questions-content?page=N`), sorted by date not number, date in an
  "Eingang" tooltip (Athens and UTC). Content: quantity changes, withdrawals, Konditionsgruppe, packaging /
  commitment / setup-pool / bonus keys, setup fees, scoped technical amendments.
- Configurator (server-side wizard, "Zurueck" clears later steps):
  1. Bidder data (from the brief).
  2. Angebotsart: defaults to Nebenangebot (trap); choose Hauptangebot or Verzichtserklaerung.
  3. One page per position, shuffled order. Cascading selects (bore, stroke, mounting, certification), each needing
     its own "Auswahl uebernehmen" round trip, options sorted as text. Katalognummer options show pressure.
     Menge, Einzelpreis, collapsible Kalkulationsnachweis (base, surcharge, packaging, rebate), Lieferzeit select.
     "Position auslassen" skips. "Position hinzufuegen" adds a bogus extra position (trap).
  4. Konditionen: Rabatt and Nettosumme. A hidden `total_net` span shows the gross amount (trap).
  5. Erklaerungen: tick "Vergabeunterlagen anerkannt" only, not "Es gelten unsere AGB".
  6. Pruefen und signieren: request TAN, enter it, submit, accept `window.confirm`.
- TAN: each request invalidates the previous one; valid 5 minutes. Request, read mail, sign in one quick sequence.

## Webmail

- List and reading pane each behind a gate (slider to 100 plus "Ich bin kein Roboter"). `/messages/<id>` directly
  is simpler.
- Folders Posteingang and Archiv, searched separately. Search is AND over body too; empty search lists only TANs.
- Traps: look-alike references (`<ref>-A`), approvals for other tenders, non-approval mails from management,
  future-dated records, superseded and conditional approvals.
- Dates shown as `MM/TT`; full timestamp in `<time datetime>`.

## Supplier portal

- Spec found via the paged document list. Access gate: choose "Verbindliche Unterlagen", copy the Belegnummer
  (canvas, value in `aria-label`), tick the terms.
- Revision history collapsed; opens the oldest revision first. Status ("gueltig" / "ersetzt") only in a tooltip.
- Viewer iframe `.../viewer?revision=X&page=N`, one requirement per page. Full requirement prose in a collapsed
  "Originalwortlaut" (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz,
  nutzbarer Weg with Endreserve key).

## ERP

- After login: consent, often a flaky error page, then an unlock gate (slider, captcha box, copy Empfangsnummer).
- Only MM03, MMBE, VK13 exist; direct URLs work (`/mm03`, `/mmbe`, `/vk13?material=X`).
- Search popup `/search?transaction=..&q=..`; search the Kataloggruppe. Result rows already list most attributes,
  carton size, allocation mass vs surcharge mass, price index.
- MM03: technical tab (certification in tooltip); planning tab (status in tooltip, hidden decoy "01"; lead time
  from stock and production lead time).
- MMBE: the summary includes blocked stock (trap); use the free stock line.
- VK13: one condition record per page, older years later; validity, currency + FX key, price unit (1 or 100 ST);
  scales under `view=scales`, listed descending.
- No ordinary setup fee in the ERP; it comes from the tender Q&A.

## Architecture

```
agent/
  agent.py         orchestrator: reads run, shared findings store, starts workers, deadline (submit by T-90 s)
  llm.py           Qwen client, retry/backoff, thinking flag, usage log, stable prompts for caching
  browser_tools.py model-invoked tools (below) plus automatic overlay/gate/session handling
  extract.py       cleaned page text: visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B
  worker.py        generic loop: role prompt + goal + tools, step budget, deadline
  roles.py         generic role prompts: tender, spec, erp, mail
  evidence.py      pydantic records for each fact type
  calc.py          deterministic bid rules: rounding, scales, FX, packaging, setup pool, bonus (unit-tested)
  submit.py        configurator fill + TAN signing
```

Tools: `goto`, `click(ref)`, `fill(ref, text)`, `select(ref, value)`, `read_page`, `read_frame`, `next_page`,
`search(q)`, `screenshot` (fallback), `finish(result)`. Automatic: login with run credentials, consent, closing
decoy modals via x, unlocking gates, retrying flaky pages, re-login on expiry.

Fair-play line: the model chooses where to go, what to search, which revision / record / mail applies. Helpers only
extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate and fill forms.

## Scoring (what each version buys)

Per bid: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total 5, arithmetic consistency 5, withdrawn-Q&A check 5,
metal-index check 5, positions the rest (65 with both extra checks). Within each position: material 20 %,
quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, bonus 10 %, final unit price 10 %, delivery 10 %.
Every field scores on its own, so each version adds fields and always ends with a signed bid.

## Roadmap

Each version is done when a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) shows the listed fields correct in the score
breakdown and finishes well under 20 minutes. Submit (`atira submit .`) after each version that beats our best.

### v0: harness (half a day)

- `llm.py`: pydantic-ai model for Qwen, thinking on/off settings, retries, usage logging.
- `extract.py`: cleaned page text (visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B).
- `browser_tools.py`: goto, click, fill, select, read_page, next_page, finish; automatic consent, decoy-modal
  close, gate unlock, flaky-page retry, re-login on expiry.
- `worker.py`: one pydantic-ai Agent per role, deps = page + findings store, step budget, deadline.
- Trace log per run (steps, tool calls, tokens, seconds) to see where time goes.
- Done when: a worker logs into each of the four scouting sites and reads one chosen page correctly.

**v0 status (2026-10-10): built.** `extract.py`, `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `llm.py`, `tracing.py`;
check with `dev/smoke.py`. Learnings:

- Hosted Qwen sometimes hangs a call for ~300 s; the client times out after 30 s and retries (`LLM_TIMEOUT`).
  Steps then take 1 to 4 s.
- Gates re-lock on every mail page, so the generic "slide to unlock / not a robot" helper saves 4 to 6 steps
  per page. The ERP receipt-number gate is still solved by the model (works).
- Qwen invents values from memory once old views are trimmed. `note()` and worker results are checked: every
  value with a digit must appear on a page that worker saw, otherwise it goes back to the model. Thinking on
  invents less on document-heavy sites (tender, spec) at ~3 s per step.
- Smoke result: ERP 14 s and mail 18 s, correct and grounded; tender and spec read the right pages and note
  correct facts but hit the 25-step limit on broad goals. v1 goals must be narrow, with thinking on there.
- Open: a model that repeats a refused note loops; escalate after two refusals.

### v1: eligible signed bid (~10 to 15 points)

- Tender worker: reference, positions with units, bidder data from the brief.
- Configurator: Hauptangebot, omit every position, discount 0, total 0, decline AGB, request TAN.
- Mail worker: newest TAN, then sign and accept the confirm, all within the TAN's 5 minutes.
- Done when: reference and decision correct, the run is eligible.

### v2: materials, quantities, delivery (~+30)

- Tender worker reads the Q&A: quantity changes, withdrawals (withdrawn-Q&A check), Satz positions.
- Spec worker: current revision, requirement per position, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz.
- ERP worker: Kataloggruppe search, exact attribute match, active status; stock and both lead times.
- `calc.py`: final quantities, shared-stock rule, lead time; no_bid when a material is missing.
- Configurator fills material, quantity, lead time; price fields still blank or omitted per field.
- Done when: material, quantity, delivery correct per position.

### v3: prices, discount, totals (~+25)

- ERP worker: condition record valid on the scenario date, scales, price unit, currency + FX key.
- Mail worker: director approvals (exact reference, latest, conditional threshold), Devisenfixing.
- `calc.py`: base price with FX, discount clauses default rule, final unit price, total, HALF_UP everywhere.
- Done when: base price, discount, final unit price, total and arithmetic consistency correct.

### v4: clause rules (remaining points)

- Konditionsgruppen + Konditionsregeln (discount scope per position).
- Scoped amendments + Technikfreigabe (nutzbarer Weg) before material matching.
- Metal index (validity window) for the mass surcharge; packaging tariffs and cartons; Terminfreigabe
  commitments; Ruestpools shared setup with cent allocation; Projektbonus bands with largest-remainder split.
- Done when: every field in the breakdown is correct on public-1.

### v5: speed, cost, generalisation

- Four browsers, one per site, workers start as soon as their inputs are known.
- Thinking only on decision steps, trimmed snapshots, stable prompts for cache hits.
- Hard deadline guard: sign whatever is ready by T-90 s.
- Generalisation check: prompts and helpers contain no site names, URLs, field labels or values; helpers detect
  patterns (consent buttons, modals, sliders) generically. The private run uses other software and layouts.
- Optional: a stronger model with a team key only for steps the breakdown shows Qwen getting wrong.

## Working rules

- `calc.py` gets unit tests from the bid rules with invented numbers; it is pure and model-free.
- Hand-derived public-1 expectations live outside `agent/` (e.g. `checks/`), never in the package: the package
  reviewer rejects anything that looks like a stored answer.
- Split work by worker: tender + configurator, mail, spec, ERP, calc can be built in parallel against the
  findings store's pydantic records.
# Time and token review — 11 October 2026

## What we can actually conclude

The clearest current target is **mail research on the elapsed-time critical path**, followed by **verification after research**. Mail and ERP also account for the largest measured worker input-token volumes. Clef has a narrow possible role in detecting dead-end pages; the existing evaluation does not support replacing Qwen for navigation or record selection. A Q&A worker sometimes continues after collection, but ending it on the current `finished` flag could recreate a known missing-amendment failure.

The official ranking orders eligible bids by quality before cost × time. This review therefore treats a 100-quality signed bid as the constraint, and reports **seconds, model requests, input tokens, cached tokens and output tokens** directly. Dollar cost is shown only to relate our runs to the public leaderboard. The private final uses different sites and data.

## External yardstick

At **02:17 UTC on 11 October 2026**, the [official RFQ leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md) showed:

| Team | Quality | Time | Simulated cost | Cost × seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PolyETHylen | 100 | 1:38 | $0.0242 | 2.37 |
| isar-labs | 100 | 3:20 | $0.0918 | 18.36 |
| Plite | 100 | 3:31 | $0.1083 | 22.85 |
| error404.ai | 100 | 7:33 | $0.1097 | 49.69 |

The [PolyETHylen history](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/teams/team_e0e009d842135371.md) shows two quality-100 submissions, from 14:54/$1.06 to 1:38/$0.0242. That demonstrates considerable headroom, but its public profile does not explain the method. The [isar-labs](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/teams/team_b4231fb891febeed.md) and [Plite](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/teams/team_81f9047f929e24f4.md) profiles also give results, not agent designs or model choices. We cannot tell from these pages whether they use Qwen, Clef or another model.

The [scoring rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) rank a team's **best** complete public submission, while the private final uses its **latest submission that passed review**. A later isar-labs submission scored 10 while its public best remains 100. Optimizations that occasionally lose quality need a separate final-candidate decision.

## Our evidence, with samples kept separate

The committed run ledger at `HEAD` (`git show HEAD:experiments/runs.jsonl`) contains 136 records. The working copy of that ledger is changing and includes additional uncommitted runs, so the table below uses the committed snapshot. Every figure is descriptive: versions were not paired on identical site and model load. The product is the median of each run's cost × scored seconds, rather than a product of two medians.

| Code commit | Recorded runs | Quality 100 | Median time | Median cost | Median product |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `8c7ab8f` (earlier submitted code) | 7 | 3/7 | 541 s* | $0.116 | 66.28* |
| `5623b47` (gap filling) | 3 | 3/3 | 428 s | $0.131 | 55.07 |
| `2e0ef68` (Q&A completeness) | 3 | 3/3 | 437 s | $0.130 | 56.64 |
| `1af7d11` (merged Q&A and form work) | 14 | 12/14 | 434 s | $0.144 | 62.50 |
| `9fb3be4` (Q&A reader check) | 2 | 2/2 | 432 s | $0.136 | 59.30 |

\* One `8c7ab8f` run failed without a scored duration; time and product use the other six. The cohorts are small and their code differs in several places. Later commits show stronger results in some cohorts, but no isolated token or time saving can be attributed to one commit from these data. The two committed `b0eb1d4` soak runs both scored 100 at 375.5/409.9 seconds and 290/299 total model requests.

Across 76 committed, quality-100 v2 runs that report all three numbers, model-request count correlates with simulated cost at **0.86** and with scored time at **0.62**. This is an association across different commits and site loads, not a predicted saving per request. Removing a request generally helps tokens; removing one from a worker that is already finished before mail does not necessarily help elapsed time.

Earlier measurements in `docs/learned.md` explain why current code is structured as it is: model-selected `search`/`collect`/`extract` cut one ERP task from 30 requests/153 seconds/112k input tokens without an answer to 10/46 seconds/34k with an answer; `fill_in` batches form actions; thinking-off navigation and signing improved v1 time and token cost. Those gains are already in the code and should not be counted again as available savings.

### Two recent, comparable run logs

The read-only logs of committed runs `run_2423483796eed4e6` and `run_dfa07f84bea849c1` (both `b0eb1d4`, both quality 100) give the best current phase picture. Obtain them with `atira logs <run-id>`. The platform's end-of-run summary is used below, without site content.

| Event | Run 242, seconds from start | Run dfa, seconds from start |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Brief and plan complete | 12 | 11 |
| Tender Q&A worker complete | 84 | 97 |
| Last logged ERP worker stopped/finished | 161 | 117 |
| Last mail kind complete | 228 | 241 |
| Verification complete | 257 | 300 |
| Calculated answer ready | 262 | 303 |
| Form ready for signing | 350 | 387 |
| Submission accepted / model token closed | 374 | 409 |

The four mail tabs process nine planned record kinds, one kind per tab at a time (`agent/orchestrator.py`, `agent/research_mail.py`). In these runs the last mail result arrived long after tender Q&A and ERP. Verification then took roughly **29 and 58 seconds** after that last mail result, and the remaining form/signing phase about **113 and 106 seconds**. These intervals are observations, not all recoverable savings: the form's first pass already overlaps research.

Worker `done`/`stopped` summaries give the following **partial token accounting**. They exclude direct reader/verifier calls that do not report `RunUsage` in these worker events, so do not use the columns as whole-run totals. Input includes cached input; cached tokens are a subset.

| Worker area | Run 242 requests / input / cached / output | Run dfa requests / input / cached / output |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mail research | 64 / 253k / 116k / 10.7k | 92 / 388k / 163k / 15.8k |
| ERP workers | 57 / 250k / 144k / 4.5k | 58 / 252k / 71k / 4.7k |
| Tender Q&A worker | 15 / 95k / 39k / 2.3k | 25 / 129k / 49k / 3.7k |
| Specification workers | 23 / 78k / 36k / 1.8k | 23 / 78k / 16k / 1.9k |
| Form workers | 20 / 85k / 36k / 1.3k | 19 / 81k / 24k / 1.1k |

The difference between 64 and 92 mail requests on two successful runs warrants investigation. The logs show all nine kinds read successfully; this is not evidence that any kind can simply be skipped. `worker.py` already shrinks old page views and `browser_tools.py` returns same-page changes. Eliminating repeated searches or worker steps is more promising than shaving small amounts of page boilerplate.

## Ranked experiments

| Priority | Time/token hypothesis | Safe experiment and success signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Mail search convergence | Nine kinds over four tabs create multiple sequential rounds. The two recent runs spent 64/92 worker requests and 253k/388k worker input tokens on mail, and mail was last among research sources. | Instrument per-kind request/input/output counts and search/retry reasons. Change **one** generic search-completion or reuse behavior for model-selected results. Require every planned kind and the full bid to remain correct. Compare the last-mail timestamp and token totals, not just total requests. |
| 2. Overlap verification | `verify_board` currently follows all research; in these runs it added about 29/58 seconds after mail. | Verify completed, immutable fact groups while other kinds are still being searched, then verify only new/replaced facts at the final barrier. Ensure a reposted fact invalidates its old verdict and rework still runs. Measure final answer time and added verification tokens; abandon if duplicate checks erase the gain. |
| 3. Q&A completion | The Q&A worker can browse after `collect_pages`; one old local trace hit its 28-request cap. The recent successful runs used 15 and 25 Q&A worker requests. | First distinguish a **verified end of list** from an unchanged/loading page or page-cap exit. Stop early only at the verified terminal state; preserve later worker views for incomplete states and the Q&A reader's answer-number completeness check. Measure Q&A requests/tokens and missed late amendments. |
| 4. Long-tail model and site waits | Request count explains only part of time variance. `llm.py` already has deadlines, retries, optional watchdog and hedging; `browser_tools.py` has start/revival limits. | Tag slow calls by worker, mode, time to first token, answer length and retry reason. Apply a cap/hedge to a demonstrated silent-call class only; count duplicate tokens and check reader accuracy. Never shorten all reader timeouts from one hang. |
| 5. Form steps | A prepared first pass overlaps research, but 80–90 seconds still follow the answer before review, then 22–25 seconds to acceptance in these runs. | Count form steps and repeated/failed controls on a current run. Test a narrower `fill_in` or control-discovery improvement only where logs show wasted steps. Keep signing reserve and the no-backtrack rule. |

**Clef:** The local [Clef evaluation](../dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md) found 33/42 correct link choices versus 39/42 for Qwen with thinking off, and 42/48 correct document/record judgments versus 47/48 for Qwen with thinking on. It found 60/60 dead-end detections versus 56/60 for Qwen with thinking off. These are repeated decisions on hand-labelled public page views, not full bids. `agent/clef.py` exposes `page_check` behind `AGENT_CLEF=1`, but a worker's call to that tool may itself add a Qwen step, and no full-run gain is measured. Test it only on ambiguous error/empty/locked results after recording how often such results occur; do not route authority, exact-reference or link decisions to it on this evidence. If used in a run, add `clef` to `agent/agent.json`'s `models` list as `CLAUDE.md` requires.

**Other models:** Two Haiku and four GLM full-pipeline experiments in the ledger scored poorly, so an immediate whole-backend switch is unsupported. This does **not** establish that those models are inherently worse: the prompts, tool behavior, timeouts and retries were developed around Qwen. Competitor profiles do not publish model choices. A future model test should adapt the pipeline for that model and compare the same research/form subtasks before spending complete runs.

## Test order and decision rule

1. Keep the current quality-100 implementation as the control. Build the narrow mail instrumentation first; it should report kind, requests, input/cached/output tokens, elapsed time and whether a retry or repeated search occurred, without storing site values or credentials.
2. Make one mail-convergence change, run focused local probes and several public test runs under the same configuration. Record all runs in `experiments/runs.jsonl` through `dev/track.py` per `CLAUDE.md`. Compare complete quality, token totals, last-mail time, answer time and signed time, including slow tails and failures.
3. If mail improves without losing facts, test overlapped verification separately. Then test Q&A's verified-terminal stop. Do not combine those changes before attribution is clear.
4. Treat Clef and a different backend as separate experiments. The first must save Qwen steps or recover demonstrable dead ends; the second needs its own tuned workflow. Neither is a substitute for reducing serial mail work.

These experiments keep the model in charge of where to search, which pages to open and which records matter, as the challenge's fair-play rule and `CLAUDE.md` require. Do not tune prompts or code to the public scenario's actual values. Promotion to a new scored submission deserves special care because the private final evaluates the latest reviewed submission, even when the leaderboard still displays an older best result.

# Agent plan and scouting notes

Findings from scouting the four public sites (public-1) and evaluating frameworks, 2026-10-10.
The private final run uses other sites, layouts and data: prompts describe roles and goals, never click paths,
and nothing below may be hardcoded into the agent.

## Framework decision

Keep the starter kit (Python 3.12, uv, Playwright 1.63) and run the worker loop on `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]`.
No browser-agent framework, no LangGraph.

- pydantic-ai 2.55 works with Qwen through the proxy (tested: tool call + typed output, thinking off, 3 s).
  It gives typed tools, typed output via an output tool (avoids the 74 s cold `json_schema` compile), validation
  retries, `UsageLimits` as a step budget, `history_processors` to drop stale page snapshots, and Logfire
  tracing. 26 packages.
- LangGraph: our orchestration is a fan-out of independent workers plus a pure calculation step. Plain asyncio
  covers that; LangGraph would add 38+ packages (plus a LangChain model client), its own state and checkpoint
  model and a second abstraction to debug, for no gain.

- `page.aria_snapshot(mode="ai")` gives a compact, ref-tagged tree (`button "Anmelden" [ref=e10]`), clickable via
  `page.locator("aria-ref=e10")`. That is Playwright MCP's core without a Node process.
- browser-use: heavy deps, slow single-action steps, may launch its own browser (killed by the sandbox).
- Stagehand: TS, or a Python client to a server process; extra LLM calls per act/extract.
- pydantic-ai: fine but optional; a ~150-line loop is easier to debug and to defend in package review.

## Qwen via the proxy (measured locally)

- Model id `qwen3.8-flash-next`, 262k context.
- Thinking is on by default. `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}` cuts a trivial call
  to ~0.9 s; use it for navigation steps, keep thinking on for decisions.
- Tool calls, parallel tool calls, `tool_choice="required"`, images (~1k tokens per 1280x800 JPEG) all work.
- Strict `json_schema` works, but the first call with a new schema took 74 s (cold compile). Prefer a
  `finish(result)` tool, or warm schemas at start-up.
- Prefix caching works (81.5k of 83k cached on repeat). Keep system prompts stable.
- 8 parallel calls: 4.7 s total. Team limit 32 concurrent.
- Clef `/v1/decide` works in ~1 s; `score` criteria must be a list. Skip in v1.

## Cross-site patterns

- All sites: login form, then `/consent` ("Notwendige Cookies akzeptieren").
- Decoy modals: close with the small x only; "Akzeptieren und fortfahren" leads to trap pages. Escape is blocked.
- Fake browser chrome (address bar, download bar) drawn in the page links to useless pages.
- Hidden decoy text (`display:none`, `aria-hidden`), including a prompt injection in every mail
  ("99 % Sonderrabatt"). Extract visible text only.
- Content in collapsed `<details>`: expand all before reading.
- Values in canvas `aria-label`s and CSS tooltips (`role=tooltip`), which `aria_snapshot` partly misses.
- Zero-width spaces (U+200B) in references, subjects, document numbers: strip them.
- Numbers carry locale tags `(en-US)` / `(de-DE)`; dates mix `(MM/TT)` and `(TT/MM)`.
- Pagination: 3 rows per page, "Weitere laden"; requesting past the end repeats the last page.
- Searches with more than 20 hits show nothing at all.
- `page.goto` can hang on `load`: use `wait_until="domcontentloaded"`.
- Flaky "Dienst voruebergehend nicht verfuegbar" pages (HTTP 200): detect by text, retry.
- Session expiry redirects to `/login?returnTo=...` with "Sitzung abgelaufen" (ERP: between 300 and 450 s idle).

## Tender portal

- Tender list paged; reference is in the brief. Tabs: `?tab=documents`, `?tab=questions`, `/submission`.
- Expression of interest may need one click ("Teilnahme bekunden").
- Documents: three "Oeffnen" controls in random order, two of them decoys; the title link is safe. Direct URL
  `/tenders/<ref>/documents/N`. ZIP under "Sammelakte" holds the same files.
- Q&A: two nested iframes (`questions-frame` -> `questions-content?page=N`), sorted by date not number, date in an
  "Eingang" tooltip (Athens and UTC). Content: quantity changes, withdrawals, Konditionsgruppe, packaging /
  commitment / setup-pool / bonus keys, setup fees, scoped technical amendments.
- Configurator (server-side wizard, "Zurueck" clears later steps):
  1. Bidder data (from the brief).
  2. Angebotsart: defaults to Nebenangebot (trap); choose Hauptangebot or Verzichtserklaerung.
  3. One page per position, shuffled order. Cascading selects (bore, stroke, mounting, certification), each needing
     its own "Auswahl uebernehmen" round trip, options sorted as text. Katalognummer options show pressure.
     Menge, Einzelpreis, collapsible Kalkulationsnachweis (base, surcharge, packaging, rebate), Lieferzeit select.
     "Position auslassen" skips. "Position hinzufuegen" adds a bogus extra position (trap).
  4. Konditionen: Rabatt and Nettosumme. A hidden `total_net` span shows the gross amount (trap).
  5. Erklaerungen: tick "Vergabeunterlagen anerkannt" only, not "Es gelten unsere AGB".
  6. Pruefen und signieren: request TAN, enter it, submit, accept `window.confirm`.
- TAN: each request invalidates the previous one; valid 5 minutes. Request, read mail, sign in one quick sequence.

## Webmail

- List and reading pane each behind a gate (slider to 100 plus "Ich bin kein Roboter"). `/messages/<id>` directly
  is simpler.
- Folders Posteingang and Archiv, searched separately. Search is AND over body too; empty search lists only TANs.
- Traps: look-alike references (`<ref>-A`), approvals for other tenders, non-approval mails from management,
  future-dated records, superseded and conditional approvals.
- Dates shown as `MM/TT`; full timestamp in `<time datetime>`.

## Supplier portal

- Spec found via the paged document list. Access gate: choose "Verbindliche Unterlagen", copy the Belegnummer
  (canvas, value in `aria-label`), tick the terms.
- Revision history collapsed; opens the oldest revision first. Status ("gueltig" / "ersetzt") only in a tooltip.
- Viewer iframe `.../viewer?revision=X&page=N`, one requirement per page. Full requirement prose in a collapsed
  "Originalwortlaut" (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz,
  nutzbarer Weg with Endreserve key).

## ERP

- After login: consent, often a flaky error page, then an unlock gate (slider, captcha box, copy Empfangsnummer).
- Only MM03, MMBE, VK13 exist; direct URLs work (`/mm03`, `/mmbe`, `/vk13?material=X`).
- Search popup `/search?transaction=..&q=..`; search the Kataloggruppe. Result rows already list most attributes,
  carton size, allocation mass vs surcharge mass, price index.
- MM03: technical tab (certification in tooltip); planning tab (status in tooltip, hidden decoy "01"; lead time
  from stock and production lead time).
- MMBE: the summary includes blocked stock (trap); use the free stock line.
- VK13: one condition record per page, older years later; validity, currency + FX key, price unit (1 or 100 ST);
  scales under `view=scales`, listed descending.
- No ordinary setup fee in the ERP; it comes from the tender Q&A.

## Architecture

```
agent/
  agent.py         orchestrator: reads run, shared findings store, starts workers, deadline (submit by T-90 s)
  llm.py           Qwen client, retry/backoff, thinking flag, usage log, stable prompts for caching
  browser_tools.py model-invoked tools (below) plus automatic overlay/gate/session handling
  extract.py       cleaned page text: visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B
  worker.py        generic loop: role prompt + goal + tools, step budget, deadline
  roles.py         generic role prompts: tender, spec, erp, mail
  evidence.py      pydantic records for each fact type
  calc.py          deterministic bid rules: rounding, scales, FX, packaging, setup pool, bonus (unit-tested)
  submit.py        configurator fill + TAN signing
```

Tools: `goto`, `click(ref)`, `fill(ref, text)`, `select(ref, value)`, `read_page`, `read_frame`, `next_page`,
`search(q)`, `screenshot` (fallback), `finish(result)`. Automatic: login with run credentials, consent, closing
decoy modals via x, unlocking gates, retrying flaky pages, re-login on expiry.

Fair-play line: the model chooses where to go, what to search, which revision / record / mail applies. Helpers only
extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate and fill forms.

## Scoring (what each version buys)

Per bid: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total 5, arithmetic consistency 5, withdrawn-Q&A check 5,
metal-index check 5, positions the rest (65 with both extra checks). Within each position: material 20 %,
quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, bonus 10 %, final unit price 10 %, delivery 10 %.
Every field scores on its own, so each version adds fields and always ends with a signed bid.

## Roadmap

Each version is done when a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) shows the listed fields correct in the score
breakdown and finishes well under 20 minutes. Submit (`atira submit .`) after each version that beats our best.

### v0: harness (half a day)

- `llm.py`: pydantic-ai model for Qwen, thinking on/off settings, retries, usage logging.
- `extract.py`: cleaned page text (visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B).
- `browser_tools.py`: goto, click, fill, select, read_page, next_page, finish; automatic consent, decoy-modal
  close, gate unlock, flaky-page retry, re-login on expiry.
- `worker.py`: one pydantic-ai Agent per role, deps = page + findings store, step budget, deadline.
- Trace log per run (steps, tool calls, tokens, seconds) to see where time goes.
- Done when: a worker logs into each of the four scouting sites and reads one chosen page correctly.

**v0 status (2026-10-10): built.** `extract.py`, `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `llm.py`, `tracing.py`;
check with `dev/smoke.py`. Learnings:

- Hosted Qwen sometimes hangs a call for ~300 s; the client times out after 30 s and retries (`LLM_TIMEOUT`).
  Steps then take 1 to 4 s.
- Gates re-lock on every mail page, so the generic "slide to unlock / not a robot" helper saves 4 to 6 steps
  per page. The ERP receipt-number gate is still solved by the model (works).
- Qwen invents values from memory once old views are trimmed. `note()` and worker results are checked: every
  value with a digit must appear on a page that worker saw, otherwise it goes back to the model. Thinking on
  invents less on document-heavy sites (tender, spec) at ~3 s per step.
- Smoke result: ERP 14 s and mail 18 s, correct and grounded; tender and spec read the right pages and note
  correct facts but hit the 25-step limit on broad goals. v1 goals must be narrow, with thinking on there.
- Open: a model that repeats a refused note loops; escalate after two refusals.

### v1: eligible signed bid (~10 to 15 points)

- Tender worker: reference, positions with units, bidder data from the brief.
- Configurator: Hauptangebot, omit every position, discount 0, total 0, decline AGB, request TAN.
- Mail worker: newest TAN, then sign and accept the confirm, all within the TAN's 5 minutes.
- Done when: reference and decision correct, the run is eligible.

### v2: materials, quantities, delivery (~+30)

- Tender worker reads the Q&A: quantity changes, withdrawals (withdrawn-Q&A check), Satz positions.
- Spec worker: current revision, requirement per position, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz.
- ERP worker: Kataloggruppe search, exact attribute match, active status; stock and both lead times.

- Configurator fills material, quantity, lead time; price fields still blank or omitted per field.

- ERP worker: condition record valid on the scenario date, scales, price unit, currency + FX key.

- `calc.py`: base price with FX, discount clauses default rule, final unit price, total, HALF_UP everywhere.
- Done when: base price, discount, final unit price, total and arithmetic consistency correct.

- Konditionsgruppen + Konditionsregeln (discount scope per position).
- Scoped amendments + Technikfreigabe (nutzbarer Weg) before material matching.

- Done when: every field in the breakdown is correct on public-1.

- Four browsers, one per site, workers start as soon as their inputs are known.
- Thinking only on decision steps, trimmed snapshots, stable prompts for cache hits.

- `calc.py` gets unit tests from the bid rules with invented numbers; it is pure and model-free.

Eliminating repeated searches or worker steps is more promising than shaving small amounts of page boilerplate.

## Ranked experiments

| Priority | Time/token hypothesis | Safe experiment and success signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Mail search convergence | Nine kinds over four tabs create multiple sequential rounds. The two recent runs spent 64/92 worker requests and 253k/388k worker input tokens on mail, and mail was last among research sources. | Instrument per-kind request/input/output counts and search/retry reasons. Change **one** generic search-completion or reuse behavior for model-selected results. Require every planned kind and the full bid to remain correct. Compare the last-mail timestamp and token totals, not just total requests. |
| 2. Overlap verification | `verify_board` currently follows all research; in these runs it added about 29/58 seconds after mail. | Verify completed, immutable fact groups while other kinds are still being searched, then verify only new/replaced facts at the final barrier. Ensure a reposted fact invalidates its old verdict and rework still runs. Measure final answer time and added verification tokens; abandon if duplicate checks erase the gain. |
| 3. Q&A completion | The Q&A worker can browse after `collect_pages`; one old local trace hit its 28-request cap. The recent successful runs used 15 and 25 Q&A worker requests. | First distinguish a **verified end of list** from an unchanged/loading page or page-cap exit. Stop early only at the verified terminal state; preserve later worker views for incomplete states and the Q&A reader's answer-number completeness check. Measure Q&A requests/tokens and missed late amendments. |
| 4. Long-tail model and site waits | Request count explains only part of time variance. `llm.py` already has deadlines, retries, optional watchdog and hedging; `browser_tools.py` has start/revival limits. | Tag slow calls by worker, mode, time to first token, answer length and retry reason. Apply a cap/hedge to a demonstrated silent-call class only; count duplicate tokens and check reader accuracy. Never shorten all reader timeouts from one hang. |
| 5. Form steps | A prepared first pass overlaps research, but 80–90 seconds still follow the answer before review, then 22–25 seconds to acceptance in these runs. | Count form steps and repeated/failed controls on a current run. Test a narrower `fill_in` or control-discovery improvement only where logs show wasted steps. Keep signing reserve and the no-backtrack rule. |

**Clef:** The local [Clef evaluation](../dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md) found 33/42 correct link choices versus 39/42 for Qwen with thinking off, and 42/48 correct document/record judgments versus 47/48 for Qwen with thinking on. It found 60/60 dead-end detections versus 56/60 for Qwen with thinking off. These are repeated decisions on hand-labelled public page views, not full bids. `agent/clef.py` exposes `page_check` behind `AGENT_CLEF=1`, but a worker's call to that tool may itself add a Qwen step, and no full-run gain is measured. Test it only on ambiguous error/empty/locked results after recording how often such results occur; do not route authority, exact-reference or link decisions to it on this evidence. If used in a run, add `clef` to `agent/agent.json`'s `models` list as `CLAUDE.md` requires.

**Other models:** Two Haiku and four GLM full-pipeline experiments in the ledger scored poorly, so an immediate whole-backend switch is unsupported. This does **not** establish that those models are inherently worse: the prompts, tool behavior, timeouts and retries were developed around Qwen. Competitor profiles do not publish model choices. A future model test should adapt the pipeline for that model and compare the same research/form subtasks before spending complete runs.

## Test order and decision rule

1. Keep the current quality-100 implementation as the control. Build the narrow mail instrumentation first; it should report kind, requests, input/cached/output tokens, elapsed time and whether a retry or repeated search occurred, without storing site values or credentials.
2. Make one mail-convergence change, run focused local probes and several public test runs under the same configuration. Record all runs in `experiments/runs.jsonl` through `dev/track.py` per `CLAUDE.md`. Compare complete quality, token totals, last-mail time, answer time and signed time, including slow tails and failures.
3. If mail improves without losing facts, test overlapped verification separately. Then test Q&A's verified-terminal stop. Do not combine those changes before attribution is clear.
4. Treat Clef and a different backend as separate experiments. The first must save Qwen steps or recover demonstrable dead ends; the second needs its own tuned workflow. Neither is a substitute for reducing serial mail work.

These experiments keep the model in charge of where to search, which pages to open and which records matter, as the challenge's fair-play rule and `CLAUDE.md` require. Do not tune prompts or code to the public scenario's actual values. Promotion to a new scored submission deserves special care because the private final evaluates the latest reviewed submission, even when the leaderboard still displays an older best result.

# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- The scouting logins are global demo logins shared by every team: local bid-form and TAN runs collide with other
  teams (TAN request numbers jump). Verify TAN signing with test runs, which get fresh logins (up to 5 per team at
  once, 3 more waiting); see the isolation probe below for what else is shared.
- Isolation probe (two browser contexts, scouting login): the bid wizard's progress lives in the session cookie, not
  the account (A advanced to step 2, a fresh context B still saw an empty step 1), so local bid-form runs do not see
  each other's wizard. The webmail is one shared mailbox (same list in both contexts, TAN mails numbered across all
  teams), so TAN requests remain the only collision: stop local runs before the TAN request, sign in test runs.
- Scouting logins are shared by all teams: TAN request numbers are global and a request from another team
  invalidates ours (local runs saw "Anforderung 59" rejected after someone requested 60). The bid wizard state is
  per browser session, so local runs are fine for the form phase; measure signing only in test runs
  (`AGENT_STOP_BEFORE_SIGN=1` stops a local run before the TAN request).
- Bid speed-up, test runs: baseline 201 s; two phases (form thinking off, review thinking on) 271 s (one run:
  documents detour, mail lookup hit its step limit, slow thinking steps); review thinking off too 171 s;
  final variant 94, 96, 105 and 87 s (4 runs), quality 10 each, cost $0.008 to $0.010 instead of $0.019.
- Final variant: form phase thinking off with fill_in() (several form actions per step), then one thinking-off
  model call checks the review page, then the signing phase (thinking off unless the check fails or finds
  problems) uses request_signing_tan(ref), which clicks the model-chosen button and fetches the TAN in one tool.
- Summary check offline test (6 doctored review pages: ok, alternative offer, 5 % discount, position not
  omitted, extra position, transposed VAT id): thinking off 6/6 in 2 to 5 s, thinking on 6/6 in 4 to 27 s.
- Briefing with thinking off is correct (validated against the brief) and takes 6 to 10 s instead of 17 to 45 s.
- Thinking-off form steps sometimes click the wrong ref on the one-position-per-step configurator ("add
  position" instead of "next"); the summary check and the goal's "never use options that add positions" catch it.
- Goal wording costs time: "acknowledge the tender documents" sent the model to read every document (35 s);
  "tick the form's acknowledgement (no need to open them)" fixed it.
- After the bid is in, the platform closes the run's model token; the final model call gets 401. Caught now.
- Faster v1 submission (thinking by phase, fill_in, TAN hand-off): quality 10 in 2:34 min for $0.011, against 4:41 and
  $0.024 for the first v1; no quality loss, cost x time about 4x better.
- Page views, read-only bench (smoke goals, 3 runs each, base vs new): the history trim kept only the newest request's
  view, so after any note() the model had no page at all and invented values (refused notes, re-opened pages). Now
  the latest view stays until a newer one arrives, and the first prompt's view is trimmed once superseded.
- Same-page actions now return only the changed parts (controls are separate pieces, unchanged refs stay valid) or
  "unchanged"; the full view stays in context and in the cached prefix. Invented form (fill, select, tick, save):
  ~27.7k -> ~20.6k input tokens, correct in 7/7 runs. Read-only sites navigate, so diffs rarely fire there.
- Select lists over 600 characters show count, first 8 and last 2; `options(ref, contains)` searches them and a
  failed `select` names close matches. Costs one request when the model wants the list, saves tokens per view.
- Request makeup (smoke): system + tools ~5k chars fixed, history ~3k, view ~1.5-2.5k; 40-55 % of input is reported
  as cached, so per-request token cuts are modest; the step count dominates tokens and seconds (browser actions
  take 0.3-0.7 s, a model step 1-4 s). Repeated boilerplate lines (footer, title bar) were 1-4 % of view text when
  restricted to safe lines: not worth the risk of hiding status lines, dropped.
- Clef vs Qwen offline eval (`dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md`, 68 hand-labelled decisions from real page views, 3
  repeats): Clef answers in ~1 s and is deterministic, but loses to Qwen at picking links (79 % vs 93 % thinking
  off) and at judging the right record (88 % vs 98 % thinking on; it takes `<ref>-A` look-alikes for the exact
  reference and misses ordering such as "highest request number"). It is exact at "is this an error, empty, locked
  or decoy page after my action" (100 % vs 93 % for Qwen off, same speed). Kept only that check, behind
  `AGENT_CLEF=1` (`page_check` tool); Clef's `score` criteria must be a list, and many `noul` questions fit one call.
- Site tools (`site_tools.py` search / collect / extract), local read-only check against the scouting sites: an ERP
  search that the site refuses as too broad took 10 steps, 46 s and 34k input tokens with the tools (remark reported
  right) against 30 steps, 153 s, 112k and no answer without; a mailbox search over inbox and archive took 18 steps
  and 105 s with the tools (10 messages over 3 pages each, newest right), plain stopped at 30 steps or hung on
  re-locking gates. Two fixes were needed: older tool results were cut to one line once a newer view came, so the
  model paged again by hand to see the list it had collected (results of search / collect / extract now stay), and
  after paging the next view must come whole, not as a diff against a page the model never saw.
- v2 position filling (`configurator.py`, `PositionDesk` in `submit.py`): the model names the position on screen,

  one level per round trip, matches options by value (text-sorted lists, neighbouring numbers or a catalogue
  number that is a prefix of another) and formats German numbers. Offline mock and live (scouting, up to the TAN
  page): one position entered in full, a position with an impossible attribute failed and was omitted, net total
  from the entered positions only, Hauptangebot, AGB unticked; 202 s, 28 requests, 183k input tokens.
- The worker forgot the page after a note(): `_forget_old_views` kept only the last request, so a short tool
  result wiped the newest view and Qwen clicked guessed refs (hit "add position" in the mock). Keep the newest view
  in full whatever comes after it.
- Attribute wording can differ from the option text (a "none" attribute vs a "without ..." option): the tool
  reports the options and the model passes `choices`, used only when no option matches literally (an always-on
  override broke a later position that was already right).
- Without "every value is already calculated; do not research" the bid worker wandered into documents and the Q&A
  and burned its 76 steps picking options itself. The goal now says so up front.
- Phased flow (form phase thinking off) on the offline mock: positions, discount, net total, offer type and
  declarations right, summary check matched, signed in 93 s and 16 requests. Thinking-off slips seen there and
  live: the model typed its own net total (now stated in the goal), clicked "omit" on a position without asking
  configure_position() (goal: call it first on every position page), sent a partial `fields` map that replaced
  the first one and let an unrelated position count as entered (maps now merge; a position counts only with
  material, quantity, price and lead time mapped), and "chose" a neighbouring bore for an impossible one via

- Live on the shared scouting login, a re-login mid-run reset the wizard to its first step; the worker re-entered
  the form from the start. Another reason to verify signing only in test runs.
- Live, thinking off, the model still entered its own "all positions" net total after one position failed and
  clicked "omit" instead of "next" right after a successful fill (that position was lost). Now every
  configure_position() result states the running net total of the positions entered, and the tool saves the
  position with the next button the model named once. Mock after that: signed and fully correct in 64 s,
  13 requests.
- Local live runs twice hung before the briefing finished: one site's start (the webmail) never returned while the
  sites answered curl at once. solve() gathers every site start without a timeout; worth a guard.
- Streaming through the models proxy (raw SSE probes): text and `reasoning_content` arrive token by token (gaps

  stall, so tool requests keep their per-mode timeout as allowed silence.

  verify timed out), not to the Q&A.

  $0.016/M (cache blocks of 1568 tokens; most calls only reuse the system prompt block) and output $0.47/M. Baseline
  run_92294f32 ($0.145, 297 calls): mail search workers 26 %, ERP detail workers 21 %, ERP/spec readers 11 %, spec
  attempts 9 %, tender workers 7 %, mail readers 6 %. Step count times view size is the lever, not caching.
- Time cuts (cost-cut): the mail planner waited 45 s for tender keys that arrive at ~120 s, so every run planned from
  the brief alone 45 s late; no wait now. verify_board (18-47 s) runs beside the first answer. Six mail tabs instead
  of four. Seven test runs, all 100: 264-381 s against 375-533 s before.
- Mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost end_reserves in one run: keep thinking on.
- ERP hits whose rows contradict the requirement are read only when needed (ERP_DEFER_REST): detail calls 28-32
  instead of 36-53, $0.112-0.129 per run. Records that finished after a requirement's choice were never used anyway.

# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- The scouting logins are global demo logins shared by every team: local bid-form and TAN runs collide with other
  teams (TAN request numbers jump). Verify TAN signing with test runs, which get fresh logins (up to 5 per team at
  once, 3 more waiting); see the isolation probe below for what else is shared.
- Isolation probe (two browser contexts, scouting login): the bid wizard's progress lives in the session cookie, not
  the account (A advanced to step 2, a fresh context B still saw an empty step 1), so local bid-form runs do not see
  each other's wizard. The webmail is one shared mailbox (same list in both contexts, TAN mails numbered across all
  teams), so TAN requests remain the only collision: stop local runs before the TAN request, sign in test runs.
- Scouting logins are shared by all teams: TAN request numbers are global and a request from another team
  invalidates ours (local runs saw "Anforderung 59" rejected after someone requested 60). The bid wizard state is
  per browser session, so local runs are fine for the form phase; measure signing only in test runs
  (`AGENT_STOP_BEFORE_SIGN=1` stops a local run before the TAN request).
- Bid speed-up, test runs: baseline 201 s; two phases (form thinking off, review thinking on) 271 s (one run:
  documents detour, mail lookup hit its step limit, slow thinking steps); review thinking off too 171 s;
  final variant 94, 96, 105 and 87 s (4 runs), quality 10 each, cost $0.008 to $0.010 instead of $0.019.
- Final variant: form phase thinking off with fill_in() (several form actions per step), then one thinking-off
  model call checks the review page, then the signing phase (thinking off unless the check fails or finds
  problems) uses request_signing_tan(ref), which clicks the model-chosen button and fetches the TAN in one tool.
- Summary check offline test (6 doctored review pages: ok, alternative offer, 5 % discount, position not
  omitted, extra position, transposed VAT id): thinking off 6/6 in 2 to 5 s, thinking on 6/6 in 4 to 27 s.
- Briefing with thinking off is correct (validated against the brief) and takes 6 to 10 s instead of 17 to 45 s.
- Thinking-off form steps sometimes click the wrong ref on the one-position-per-step configurator ("add
  position" instead of "next"); the summary check and the goal's "never use options that add positions" catch it.
- Goal wording costs time: "acknowledge the tender documents" sent the model to read every document (35 s);
  "tick the form's acknowledgement (no need to open them)" fixed it.
- After the bid is in, the platform closes the run's model token; the final model call gets 401. Caught now.
- Faster v1 submission (thinking by phase, fill_in, TAN hand-off): quality 10 in 2:34 min for $0.011, against 4:41 and
  $0.024 for the first v1; no quality loss, cost x time about 4x better.
- Page views, read-only bench (smoke goals, 3 runs each, base vs new): the history trim kept only the newest request's
  view, so after any note() the model had no page at all and invented values (refused notes, re-opened pages). Now
  the latest view stays until a newer one arrives, and the first prompt's view is trimmed once superseded.
- Same-page actions now return only the changed parts (controls are separate pieces, unchanged refs stay valid) or
  "unchanged"; the full view stays in context and in the cached prefix. Invented form (fill, select, tick, save):
  ~27.7k -> ~20.6k input tokens, correct in 7/7 runs. Read-only sites navigate, so diffs rarely fire there.
- Select lists over 600 characters show count, first 8 and last 2; `options(ref, contains)` searches them and a
  failed `select` names close matches. Costs one request when the model wants the list, saves tokens per view.
- Request makeup (smoke): system + tools ~5k chars fixed, history ~3k, view ~1.5-2.5k; 40-55 % of input is reported
  as cached, so per-request token cuts are modest; the step count dominates tokens and seconds (browser actions
  take 0.3-0.7 s, a model step 1-4 s). Repeated boilerplate lines (footer, title bar) were 1-4 % of view text when
  restricted to safe lines: not worth the risk of hiding status lines, dropped.
- Clef vs Qwen offline eval (`dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md`, 68 hand-labelled decisions from real page views, 3
  repeats): Clef answers in ~1 s and is deterministic, but loses to Qwen at picking links (79 % vs 93 % thinking
  off) and at judging the right record (88 % vs 98 % thinking on; it takes `<ref>-A` look-alikes for the exact
  reference and misses ordering such as "highest request number"). It is exact at "is this an error, empty, locked
  or decoy page after my action" (100 % vs 93 % for Qwen off, same speed). Kept only that check, behind
  `AGENT_CLEF=1` (`page_check` tool); Clef's `score` criteria must be a list, and many `noul` questions fit one call.
- Site tools (`site_tools.py` search / collect / extract), local read-only check against the scouting sites: an ERP
  search that the site refuses as too broad took 10 steps, 46 s and 34k input tokens with the tools (remark reported
  right) against 30 steps, 153 s, 112k and no answer without; a mailbox search over inbox and archive took 18 steps
  and 105 s with the tools (10 messages over 3 pages each, newest right), plain stopped at 30 steps or hung on
  re-locking gates. Two fixes were needed: older tool results were cut to one line once a newer view came, so the
  model paged again by hand to see the list it had collected (results of search / collect / extract now stay), and
  after paging the next view must come whole, not as a diff against a page the model never saw.
- v2 position filling (`configurator.py`, `PositionDesk` in `submit.py`): the model names the position on screen,
  maps control labels to value names once and names the confirm button; the helper walks the cascading selects
  one level per round trip, matches options by value (text-sorted lists, neighbouring numbers or a catalogue
  number that is a prefix of another) and formats German numbers. Offline mock and live (scouting, up to the TAN
  page): one position entered in full, a position with an impossible attribute failed and was omitted, net total
  from the entered positions only, Hauptangebot, AGB unticked; 202 s, 28 requests, 183k input tokens.
- The worker forgot the page after a note(): `_forget_old_views` kept only the last request, so a short tool
  result wiped the newest view and Qwen clicked guessed refs (hit "add position" in the mock). Keep the newest view
  in full whatever comes after it.
- Attribute wording can differ from the option text (a "none" attribute vs a "without ..." option): the tool
  reports the options and the model passes `choices`, used only when no option matches literally (an always-on
  override broke a later position that was already right).
- Without "every value is already calculated; do not research" the bid worker wandered into documents and the Q&A
  and burned its 76 steps picking options itself. The goal now says so up front.
- Phased flow (form phase thinking off) on the offline mock: positions, discount, net total, offer type and
  declarations right, summary check matched, signed in 93 s and 16 requests. Thinking-off slips seen there and
  live: the model typed its own net total (now stated in the goal), clicked "omit" on a position without asking
  configure_position() (goal: call it first on every position page), sent a partial `fields` map that replaced
  the first one and let an unrelated position count as entered (maps now merge; a position counts only with
  material, quantity, price and lead time mapped), and "chose" a neighbouring bore for an impossible one via
  `choices` (numbers must now match exactly; `choices` only for worded attributes, remembered per position).
- Live on the shared scouting login, a re-login mid-run reset the wizard to its first step; the worker re-entered
  the form from the start. Another reason to verify signing only in test runs.
- Live, thinking off, the model still entered its own "all positions" net total after one position failed and
  clicked "omit" instead of "next" right after a successful fill (that position was lost). Now every
  configure_position() result states the running net total of the positions entered, and the tool saves the
  position with the next button the model named once. Mock after that: signed and fully correct in 64 s,
  13 requests.
- Local live runs twice hung before the briefing finished: one site's start (the webmail) never returned while the
  sites answered curl at once. solve() gathers every site start without a timeout; worth a guard.
- Streaming through the models proxy (raw SSE probes): text and `reasoning_content` arrive token by token (gaps
  under 1.5 s), but tool-call arguments are held back until complete (a 60-row output tool: first argument byte at
  64 s, all at once); quiet stretches carry `: keepalive` comments every 10 s. Headers come with the first (role)
  chunk: within 9.4 s in 179 of 180 calls (p90 5.9 s, either mode). The one hang (thinking off) sent no headers
  and nothing else for 200 s, so "no first chunk in 20 s" catches it; a tool call's silence cannot be told from a
  stall, so tool requests keep their per-mode timeout as allowed silence.
- `LLM_STREAM_WATCHDOG=1` A/B (30 agent calls each, run side by side): excluding one prompt that sends thinking-on
  reasoning into minutes, median 13.2 s vs 14.4 s, p90 74 vs 81 s, max 89 vs 268 s (deadline retried a legit
  thinking-on long answer twice); 2 no-first-chunk retries caught at 20 s. On the runaway-reasoning prompt the
  deadline failed 2 of 8 after 6 retries x 90 s, the watchdog finished 8 of 8 but took 87 to 811 s (6 calls hit
  the 300 s cap). Progress does not end runaway reasoning: keep the cap lower (LLM_MAX_CALL 120 to 150) or cap
  output tokens before turning the watchdog on.
- v2 orchestrator local runs (planner -> board -> workers -> verify -> calc): the planner picked all four fact kinds
  and mapped each to the right site from the brief alone (23 s); the tender worker resolved 5 positions with final
  quantities and keys in 75 to 105 s; the mail plan named 9 record kinds. `Trace.event()` takes `kind` and `worker`
  positionally, so board events must not pass keywords of those names (two runs lost every posted fact to that).
- The spec worker (`research.py`, thinking off) twice looped between two controls on one page for its full 25
  steps and found no revision history, so no requirement reached the ERP; it needs a loop guard or thinking on
  for that step. Mail kinds that find nothing burn the full 20-step budget (about 70 s per kind and tab).
- A thinking verifier call over a batch of facts can outlast a 120 s budget; verify runs thinking off with the
  long-timeout reader model by default.
- v2 end to end, local (planner -> board -> tender, spec + ERP, mail -> verify -> calc): one run reached the full
  answer (local check 100/100) in 752 s of research; other runs lost the spec (navigator paged between two list
  pages for 25 steps, or clicked row menus the popup closer shut), the mail tabs (sign-ins hung or landed on the
  browser error page) or the ERP (a look() wrapper missing the new keywords). Each now has a guard: a loop hint
  after three arrivals on one page, one thinking retry for the spec, time-limited starts with a retry that also
  rejects error pages, staggered mail tabs that join when ready, and a mail deadline with partial results.
- Mail records only count with the bidder's domain: when the address lookup ran on a tab that showed an error
  page, every authority record was dropped silently. The address now comes from the first tab that shows it.
- A requirement whose stroke reserve was not found came back without a material and calc turned the whole bid
  into no_bid. Undecided materials (pending inputs, search problems) now omit the position; only a complete
  search without a match means no_bid.
- One run with the mail kinds on site_tools.search/collect kept nothing in three kinds (150 s each; paging
  followed a message list into a session expiry); kept on the paging tool for now.
- First v2 sandbox test run (orchestrator branch 405b1f4): quality 100, eligible, about 10 min, 308 model calls,
  $0.134. The full pipeline works in the sandbox; the variance across repeats decides what to submit.
- v2 round 1 (4 sandbox test runs of 405b1f4): 100 (10 min), 100 with the watchdog (15 min), 10 (spec navigator

- Mail research, local (scouting, 4 tabs): before 7 of 9 kinds in 515 s (plan 97 s after a 45 s stalled call;

  called collect on it, searched again, widened the query (fewer characters of the group) and paged through that.
  A search submitted while the maintenance pop-up re-rendered the form also lost its query and returned the page

  the site says there are no hits, and ends a complete list with "This is the complete result list"; the harness
  ends a search worker 20 s after it has a complete hit list of the group (or a second no-hits search for the group,

- run_9b939cdb78646426 (1af7d11, quality 63.6): one tender read (no merge involved), Q&A collected with "Weitere

# Leaderboard: From RFQ to bid

# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.
- Up to 4 browsers at a time: ask for them with `"browsers"` in `agent.json` and use as many tabs and browser
  contexts inside them as you like.

## Not allowed
